transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Location: Zoom

Attendees:
- Maya Patel (Redwood, AE)
- Ethan Liu (Redwood, SE)
- Jared Cole (Peregrine, CTO)
- Sana Mehta (Peregrine, Head of Security)
- Luis Ortega (Peregrine, Platform Eng)

--- Auto Summary (auto-gen, may be short) ---
Maya: Quick review of Peregrine's SSO and provisioning needs, scope for pilot, next steps to share artifacts.

00:00:07 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account, with Ethan our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:00:12 Jared: Good, thanks. Excited to dig in.
00:00:16 Ethan: Great. Today we want to cover how you'd wire up SAML for SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and then talk RBAC patterns — just-in-time access, least privilege, auditability and encryption keys.
00:00:30 Sana: Our primary concerns are audit logs for compliance, cert rotation, and ensuring minimal blast radius for dev teams. Also we have a requirement to keep EU customer PII in EU region.
00:00:45 Luis: And for platform we care about automatic provisioning from Okta and reducing manual role assignments, we can't have support tickets for every new engineer.

00:01:05 Ethan: Cool. High level — Redwood can operate hosted, dedicated, or private VPC. For Peregrine we discussed private VPC earlier — so the flow is typical SAML SP integration, we provide SP metadata, you configure IdP (Okta) and enable SCIM to sync groups and user attributes.
00:01:23 Jared: One quick Q — can SCIM do group-to-role mapping or do we need a middleware?
00:01:30 Maya: Short answer: we support SCIM group push. You can map groups to RBAC roles in the Console. Ethan, maybe show the mapping options?
00:01:38 Ethan: Yeah. So in Console you create role slices — e.g., infra-admin, app-deploy, read-only-qa — and map an incoming SCIM group to one or more roles. You can also do just-in-time elevation using a short TTL token if you want supervised escalation.
00:01:55 Sana: JIT? Can you define the audit trail there? We need to know who elevated and why.
00:02:03 Ethan: Absolutely. JIT elevation is logged as an event with user, actor, reason (free-text), duration, and the originating session. Those events are shipped to your audit log stream — we support S3, or you can push to your SIEM via HTTPS sink.
00:02:20 Luis: What's the retention by default? We have a 7-year retention requirement for certain logs.
00:02:26 Maya: By default we keep 90 days in Console. Long-term retention is an add-on where logs are exported to your S3 bucket or to Azure Blob with lifecycle rules. We'll include retention costs in the pilot estimate.
00:02:38 Jared: Ok. On encryption — if we run in VPC/on-prem we want customer-managed keys. How do you integrate with KMS or HSM?
00:02:49 Ethan: We support both. For cloud VPC we can use your AWS KMS CMKs via a cross-account grant; for on-prem or HSM we'll integrate via a KMIP-compatible HSM or customer KMS proxy. Key rotation is supported and we keep an audit trail of key usage.
00:03:05 Sana: Is the private control plane still touching plaintext? We're very sensitive about data residency and scope for SOC 2.
00:03:12 Maya: Good question. For Private deployments the control plane can be configured to not persist user payloads; we can also enable end-to-end encryption options where the platform doesn't have plaintext — but that impacts features like indexing and certain optimizations. We documented tradeoffs in the security playbook we'll send.
00:03:30 Ethan: To add — if you go with Dedicated with customer-managed KMS, inference payloads are encrypted at rest and in transit; and you can enforce network policies so only your VPC subnets can reach the instances.

00:03:50 Jared: For SAML cert rotation — can we rotate certs without downtime?
00:03:55 Ethan: Yes, we support dual certs in metadata to allow graceful rollover. You upload the new cert while old remains valid for a short overlap window. We also support automatic metadata fetch for some IdPs but recommend manual upload with rotation schedule.
00:04:10 Sana: Any gotchas on Okta SCIM attributes? We've had mismatched emails vs login names cause duplicates before.
00:04:18 Ethan: We usually recommend mapping by immutable user ID (Okta user.id) and pushing email as an attribute. Make sure to disable username-based canonicalization. We'll share a recommended mapping: id, userName, active, emails, groups, and an enterpriseExtension for tenant_id.
00:04:38 Luis: Can SCIM push deprovision events immediately? We need terminated users to lose access within 5 minutes ideally.
00:04:45 Ethan: SCIM push is near real-time but depends on your IdP. Okta group push is usually within seconds to a minute. If you need sub-minute guarantees we can use a webhook-based reprovisioning hook from your HR system as a fallback.

00:05:10 Maya: Let's go through an example: New hire is added in Okta, Okta pushes user + group via SCIM, group maps to role 'dev-sandbox-read' — the user gets access immediately. If you want JIT for 'deploy' role, the user requests elevation and gets a 15-minute token after approval.
00:05:28 Jared: For approvals — can managers approve inside Redwood or does it need to be in Okta?
00:05:33 Ethan: We support both flows. Approvals can be inside Console which then calls back to Okta for group membership change, or you can keep approvals in Okta with SCIM-based group change as the source of truth. The Console approvals give richer audit details.

00:05:55 Sana: About SOC 2 — does Redwood provide the entire SOC 2 report if we sign an NDA?
00:06:01 Maya: Yes, we can provide the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA, plus our ISO attestation documents. We'll attach those to the follow-up package.
00:06:07 Jared: Great. Can you summarize how RBAC is enforced at runtime? If someone tries to call inference APIs with an expired role, what's the behavior?
00:06:16 Ethan: Token evaluation is done at the gateway — we check the role claims against the route policy. If the role is expired, request is rejected with 401 and an event is emitted to audit stream. We also have a fallback policy option where requests can hit a lower-permission model variant for graceful degradation.
00:06:36 Luis: Interesting — that fallback could be useful for availability. Is that per-route?
00:06:40 Ethan: Yes, fallbacks are configurable per route or per model. You can set fallback to 'queue', 'lower-tier-model', or 'reject'.

00:07:00 Maya: I want to call out the default RBAC model we recommend for orgs your size: four role slices — org-admin, infra, app-owner, read-only. Keep privilege boundary between infra and app-owner to prevent lateral privilege.
00:07:14 Sana: We need least privilege for support. Support shouldn't be able to access production keys or customer payloads.
00:07:20 Ethan: You can scope support roles to console-only, with masked logs and truncated payloads. For deeper access, require an additional escalation workflow with multi-approver.

00:07:40 Jared: How about multi-tenant isolation for their EU customers? Do you offer region, or per-tenant encryption keys?
00:07:47 Maya: We provide region-specific deployments and support per-tenant encryption keys as a premium. For many customers, region isolation + data residency controls are sufficient; for stricter requirements we recommend Dedicated + CMK per-tenant.

00:08:05 Luis: On exportability — we want a copy of the audit trail exported daily to our secure bucket. Is that easy?
00:08:11 Ethan: Yes, export to S3 with server-side encryption and lifecycle rules. You can also configure retention and automatic deletion after X years. We'll provide a CloudFormation snippet for the S3 bucket policy to restrict access.

00:08:30 Sana: Can you search logs for PII? We need PII redaction.
00:08:34 Ethan: We redact PII by default from Console views. Raw exported logs can be routed to your DLP pipeline first; we also offer a redaction plugin that can redact sensitive fields before persistence.

00:08:55 Maya: Let's pivot to the pilot scope. We propose a 2-week staging pilot: integrate Okta SAML+SCIM, map three roles, run simulated provisioning flows, and run throughput tests at your typical load. Any objections?
00:09:09 Jared: That works. Timeline wise, we have an internal compliance review the week after next. If pilot runs this week and we pass review, we can scope Dedicated by end of month.
00:09:19 Maya: Good. We'll need a staging Okta integration details and a small staging VPC. Ethan, any infra notes?
00:09:26 Ethan: For staging we recommend a 3-node Dedicated cluster sized for your avg qps — I'll send sizing calc. Also propose to enable audit export to their staging S3 and a short retention window for the pilot.

00:09:40 Luis: About cert pinning and rotation in our CI — can we automate the metadata upload?
00:09:46 Ethan: We have an API for metadata upload and cert rotate; we can wire it into your CI/CD pipeline. We'll share sample scripts.

00:09:58 Sana: A few security nitty-grittys — how do you protect the admin console with SSO session lifetime? We need sessions to expire after 15 minutes of inactivity for admin roles.
00:10:09 Ethan: Session policies are configurable per role. You can set session TTLs down to 5 minutes for high-priv roles. We also recommend step-up auth (MFA) for escalation flows.

00:10:28 Maya: We're getting near the tech Q&A bit, maybe open the floor.
00:10:33 Jared: What's the expected lag for group sync when a user changes groups in Okta? You said near real-time but earlier you mentioned Okta delays. Can you quantify?
00:10:41 Ethan: Realistically, Okta group push is typically 5-30s, nominally under a minute. For very large directories it can stretch, but there's a change log you can poll if you need deterministic timing.
00:10:53 Luis: If a user is deprovisioned, do you also garbage collect cached KV entries to prevent stale access?
00:11:01 Ethan: Great point. We flush KV cache entries when role revocation is detected; there can be a tiny window depending on cache TTL, but we proactively invalidate session tokens. We can set short KV TTLs for sensitive routes.

00:11:22 Sana: Regarding attestations — when you run pen tests, can we get the findings or at least a high level summary?
00:11:28 Maya: Yes, we can share redacted summaries and remediation plans. Full detailed reports are often under NDA but we can provide the part relevant to platform security posture.

00:11:40 Ethan: Any concerns about network egress? For customers with strict egress controls we support VPC endpoints and private peering.
00:11:48 Jared: We'll likely require VPC endpoints. Also need to know which IP ranges to allow for monitoring hops.
00:11:54 Ethan: We'll produce a minimal allowlist and health-check IPs.

00:12:10 Maya: Quick compliance checklist — SAML+SCIM integration, SOC 2 under NDA, KMS/CMK support, audit export, role mapping docs, pilot SOW. We'll send that as an email and include a short checklist for your compliance team.
00:12:25 Sana: Perfect. For the pilot acceptance criteria — we need: 1) SCIM provisioning works end-to-end, 2) deprovision within 5 minutes, 3) audit logs accessible in S3 and searchable, 4) private key usage logged.
00:12:38 Maya: Noted — we'll include those as acceptance items in the pilot SOW.

00:12:50 Jared: Any limitations on SCIM — do you support nested groups?
00:12:54 Ethan: SCIM v2 doesn't standardize nested groups well; we support explicit group push and can flatten nested groups into attribute mappings during import. We'll include a helper script.

00:13:10 Luis: What about rate limits on SCIM? If you push a lot of users at once, will you see throttling?
00:13:15 Ethan: There's a rate limit but it's generous for normal orgs. For bulk imports we recommend using bulk endpoints or offline CSV import we provide.

00:13:30 Sana: Can we get an architecture diagram that annotates where encryption keys live and where logs flow? That helps our auditors.
00:13:36 Maya: Absolutely — we'll send a diagram and a minimal network topology for the VPC deployment.

00:13:50 Jared: Last question — do you offer role reviews or automated least-privilege suggestions?
00:13:57 Ethan: We do. Redwood Optimize includes role suggestion analysis that looks at actual API calls and suggests role slices based on observed entitlements. It's an add-on but helps reduce over-privilege.

00:14:12 Maya: Ok wrapping up — recap of next steps: Maya will send SOC2 + ISO pack and SAML metadata link; Ethan will share SCIM mapping template, sizing calc, and pilot playbook; Sana to share required audit fields and retention policy; we schedule the staging pilot start next Monday if Okta details are ready.
00:14:33 Jared: Sounds good. We'll aim to provide staging Okta and VPC creds by Friday.
00:14:38 Maya: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
00:14:40 End meeting.
